name: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah

phases.title: Both armies form up in four divisions
phases.text: The Sasanian army crossed the canal before dawn and drew up in four divisions with the river at its back. The Rashidun army stood in four corps about 500 metres away, with Muslim cavalry at the rear of each.

phases.title: Elephants and archers press the Muslim right
phases.text: The Persian left wing attacked the Muslim right wing with heavy arrow fire, and the elephants led the charge. Jareer's cavalry was stopped by the Sasanian heavy cavalry, and the Muslim infantry began to fall back.

phases.title: The Muslim right counterattacks
phases.text: Reinforcing infantry from the right centre and a cavalry regiment under Al-Ash'ath joined the right wing. The infantry attacked from the front and the cavalry from the flank, and the Sasanian left wing retreated.

phases.title: The Persian right and its elephants drive back the left
phases.text: Rustam then sent his right centre and right wing forward after heavy arrow fire, with the elephants in the lead. The Muslim cavalry on the left, already in panic at the elephants, was driven back.

phases.title: The elephants are turned back
phases.text: Asim's archers shot the men on the elephants and his infantry cut the saddle girths. The elephants were withdrawn, the Persian right centre and right wing retreated, and the Muslims counterattacked.

phases.title: Sa'd orders a second counterattack
phases.text: By afternoon the Persian attacks on the Muslim left had been beaten back. Sa'd ordered another counterattack and the Muslim cavalry charged from the flanks. Rustam went into the fray himself and the attacks were repulsed.

phases.title: The elephants are driven off the field
phases.text: On the third day the Muslims blinded the elephants and severed their trunks until they were driven off. The frightened elephants rushed through the Sasanian ranks towards the river, and by noon none were left on the field.

phases.title: Qa'qa leads the left centre forward
phases.text: The elephants had been driven from the field on 18 November. On the fourth day the Muslim left centre surged forward and the other corps followed. By noon Qa'qa and his men had pierced the Sasanian centre but could not break the army.

phases.title: The Sasanian right wing counterattacks
phases.text: The Sasanian right wing counterattacked and regained its lost position. The Muslim left wing retreated to its original position, and the left centre, denied its support, also fell back to where it had stood.

phases.title: The Sasanian front collapses
phases.text: After a last stand the Sasanian front gave way. Part of the army retreated in order and the rest in panic towards the river, while Jalinus held the bridgehead and brought the bulk across. The Muslim cavalry pursued.

note: The plan shows the fighting of 16 and 19 November 636; the fighting of 17 and 18 November is not drawn. The Rashidun army faced north-east and the Sasanian army south-west with the river at its back, here turned to left and right. The Sasanian rear guard under Piruzan is drawn but not followed, the Syrian reinforcements are not drawn, and the elephants, said to number about 33 and to stand eight with each division, are drawn as one body. The accounts of Rustam's death differ, and the plan does not show it.
